'''''Lilium pensylvanicum''''' is an Asian plant species of the family [[Liliaceae]]. Sometimes called the '''Siberian lily,''' it is native to a cold climate and needs frost in the winter. It is found in the wild form in [[Siberia]], the [[Russian Far East]], Mongolia, northeast China, Korea and [[Hokkaido|Hokkaidō]].<ref name = Kew/><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200027711 Flora of China, Vol. 24 Page 140 <big>毛百合</big> mao bai he ''Lilium dauricum'' Ker Gawler, Bot. Mag. 30: t. 1210. 1809. ]</ref>

The Latin name is misleading due to an error by the botanist [[John Bellenden Ker Gawler|John Bellenden Ker]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/471840#page/217/mode/1up Ker Gawler, John Bellenden 1805.  Botanical Magazine 22: plate 872 + 2 subsequent text pages] description in Latin, commentary in English, full-page color illustration</ref>

==Description==
''Lilium pensylvanicum'' reaches a height of {{convert|30|-|70|cm}} and has a width up to {{convert|25|cm|abbr=on|0}}. The stem is hard, smooth and straight, the leaves linear to lanceolate, {{convert|4|-|5|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3|-|4|mm}} wide. The plant flowers in June and July with one to six upright, dish-shaped flowers. The flower consists of six tepals curving backward from the center. The seeds mature from August to September. The bulb is roundish with a diameter of about {{convert|2|cm|abbr=on}}.

==Distribution in Japan==
''Lilium pensylvanicum'' is abundant in the wild form in the [[Notsuke Peninsula]]. Near the city of [[Betsukai, Hokkaido|Betsukai]], during July, in the "gardens of the flock of gruyas" there may be seen many photographers looking for the best snapshots of the flowering of the ''{{lang|ja-Latn|ezosukashiyuri}}'', as this species is known in [[Japanese language|Japanese]]. The city [[Koshimizu, Hokkaido|Koshimizu]], on the island of Hokkaidō, is known as the city of the ''ezosukashiyuri'' flowers. In the [[Ainu language]], the flowers are called ''{{lang|ain|masarorunpe}}'' and that is also the traditional Ainu oil lamp made from a large mussel shell and supported on a three-forked stick.<ref>[http://www.ainu-museum.or.jp アイヌ民族博物館（白老町） Ainu Museum] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002202120/http://www.ainu-museum.or.jp/ |date=2018-10-02 }} in Japanese</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.post.japanpost.jp/kitte_hagaki/stamp/furusato/2004/h160205_f.html |title=平成16年ふるさと切手「北海道遺産II」の発行 Japan Post}} in Japanese</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Lilium pensylvanicum'' is very undemanding and is easily cultivated. It is sensitive only in relation to drought. Thus the plant is popular in European and American gardens.
